ev.q: From 2022 to 2023, estimated measles cases increased 20% worldwide, from 8,645,000 to 10,341,000
Estimated measles deaths decreased 8%, from 116,800 in 2022 to 107,500 in 2023
MCV1 coverage improved to 83% in 2022 but was unchanged in 2023.
In 2023, MCV1 coverage was 64% in low-income countries, 86% in middle-income countries, and 94% in high-income countries
it was 67% and 89% in countries with and without FCV settings, respectively
The Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030) includes measles elimination as a core indicator of impact of immunization programs
During 2000–2019, estimated MCV1 coverage increased worldwide from 71% to 86%, then declined to 81% in 2021
This report describes measles elimination progress during 2000–2023.

methods_quotes.q: Because routine surveillance data typically underestimate measles cases, measles cases and deaths were estimated using a previously described model
State-space model of unobserved measles incidence during 2000–2023 generated using the following data from all WHO countries
Deaths prevented by vaccination are estimated by the area between estimated deaths with vaccination and those without vaccination.
Any country not reporting measles cases for that year was removed from the numerator and denominator when calculating incidence.
The measles mortality model used to generate estimated measles cases and deaths is rerun each year
